display.title: Chassidus Class 32: The Virtue of the Poor Man, Tzedakah and Rosh Hashanah (Elul)
display.summary_short: A Chassidus class, mostly in English, given in Elul: why Dovid HaMelech called himself poor, how tzedakah is Hashem's loan, and how Rosh Hashanah is the 'head' of the whole year.
display.summary_long: A Chassidus class taught mostly in English with Yiddish and Hebrew, given in early Elul with Rosh Hashanah approaching. The recording begins mid-lesson on the difference between a chassid and an ani (poor man), and why Dovid HaMelech pleaded before Hashem as one who is poor. The Zohar teaches that the prayer of the poor man and the prayer of Moshe are equal, and the tefillin shel yad, called the 'prayer of the poor', is put on before the tefillin shel rosh. The class then turns to tzedakah: 'one who is gracious to the poor lends to Hashem'. A rich man only holds Hashem's money in trust, Hashem refills what he gives, and the poor man does more for the giver than the giver does for him. Every mitzvah refines a person's character. A listener asks how much one must give, which leads to a discussion of working a normal day and giving a tenth or a fifth. Also included: a story of a pledge made before the Frierdiker Rebbe, Rosh Hashanah as the 'head' that directs the whole year, a personal memory of the Frierdiker Rebbe weeping before the shofar in 1943-44, giving and receiving through the chain of worlds, and emunah as the cement that holds Yiddishkeit together. The recording ends mid-sentence.
display.lesson: Give tzedakah with trust that the money is Hashem's and He repays it; the poor man who receives does even more for the giver.
